messages:
Maya Patel: hey all, onboarding question. tried to open Console (staging) -> Feature Flags and got a 403. need to toggle a flag for a partner walkthrough in ~90m. who can help with temporary access? :grimacing:
Ethan Cho: welcome Maya! :wave: what's your console email? staging only ok?
Maya Patel: maya.patel@redwood.com. staging only is fine. demo is 14:00 UTC. error shows: `{"error":"403","message":"insufficient_permissions"}`
AccessBot: Request logged (REQ-4598). Pre-check: user exists, no active elevated roles. Sent approval request to Lina Torres and Maya's manager.
Lina Torres: I can approve staging for 2 hours. @Ethan do we prefer issuing a time-limited role or a temporary service token for this case?
Ethan Cho: role is fine and hits audit logs automatically. I'll do a 2-hour grant.
OnboardingBot: FYI — added a checklist item to Maya's onboarding doc: "how to request temporary staging access for demos".
Ethan Cho: granted `feature_flags_admin (staging)` to maya.patel@redwood.com, expires in 2h (REQ-4598). confirm you can access the flag list now. :white_check_mark:
Maya Patel: I can see flags now and toggled the partner_demo flag. thanks! quick question: how do I check who owns that flag so I can request a permanent change later?
Lina Torres: click the flag, Owner field is at top-right. or CLI: `rfctl flags describe partner_demo --env staging --output json` which shows owner and last modified.
Maya Patel: awesome, saved. also where should I log the demo change for the runbook?
Ethan Cho: add a short note to the Flag Change log doc (Confluence link) and paste the audit id (REQ-4598) so security can trace it.
Maya Patel: done. appreciate the quick help everyone 389 :pray
Lina Torres: welcome aboard Maya! ping #new-hires if you need anything else.
